title: incident-bot: on-call diagnostics helpers + SLO toolkit utilities for automated runbook linking
author: Aisha Kapoor
release_notes: Adds helper utilities for richer on-call diagnostics and SLO toolkit integrations; no customer-facing API changes; improves automated runbook linking and context enrichment for incidents.
description: Context: On-call responders lack fast, high-signal links to runbooks and SLO context during incidents. This PR adds a set of helper utilities in incident-bot and the SLO toolkit to enrich on-call diagnostics messages with prioritized runbook links, SLO metadata, and quick-action helpers. Motivation: reduce mean time to resolution by surfacing the most relevant runbooks and SLO context automatically in the incident flow. Summary of changes: 1) incident-bot: add diagnostics/helpers.go which exposes a small API to score and format runbook links based on SLO impact, recent incident history, and playbook tags; 2) slo-toolkit: add utilities/slo_enrichment.go to fetch and normalize SLO metadata (owner, thresholds, runbook pointers) and a lightweight caching layer to reduce control-plane calls; 3) message templates: update templates/oncall_summary.tmpl to include prioritized links and a compact actionable menu (ack/reassign/notify); 4) observability: add metrics incident_bot.runbook_suggestions and incident_bot.slo_lookup_latency and tracing spans for enrichment flows; 5) tests: unit and integration tests for scoring heuristics and end-to-end smoke test in ci/workflows/oncall-enrichment.yaml. Checklist: - [x] Feature implemented - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration smoke tests added - [x] Documentation updated (docs/oncall/runbook-enrichment.md) - [x] Backward compatible - [x] Metrics and traces added Implementation notes: The runbook scoring algorithm is intentionally conservative: it favors SLO severity (p99 breach > error budget burn), playbook recency, and explicit tag matching from alert metadata. A short caching TTL (30s) is used to avoid stale links during short incident storms but still reduce API load. The change does not alter incident-bot's public webhook schema; it only enriches messages server-side. Testing and CI: CI run included unit test suite (pkg/*_test.go) and the new workflow which spins a lightweight SLO mock and validates that the suggested runbooks appear in the enriched message. All CI checks passed after addressing an initial flaky test (slo_enrichment_test.go) by increasing test-resilience with retry/backoff. Rollout plan: feature behind a feature flag (oncall.runbook_enrichment) defaulted to false. Steps: 1) merge with flag off, 2) enable for internal SRE canary team, 3) monitor incident_bot.runbook_suggestions and error rates for 48h, 4) enable org-wide. Migration: customers running private deployments with pinned incident-bot versions must opt-in to the new SLO toolkit integrations; documentation provides a migration section. Related: ENG-3421 (oncall diagnostics), ENG-3499 (slo toolkit caching); SUP-8812 (customer support ticket where missing runbook links delayed response).
